problem: Journal stores latest state per entity, replay intersects current grant fields by matter rather than grant lineage. Narrow then broaden, or remove then regrant, may overwrite evidence of irreversible saved-copy redaction and resurrect pre-restriction copied fields on restore. Must inspect final SQL and reproduce with old snapshot and latest journal, retaining unaffected recipients.
proposedInvestigation: Use isolated recovery-journal test flow; before snapshot paid saved details; narrow/regrant afterwards; latest journal replay must not restore redacted saved details or old task permissions. Do not implement speculative global revoke.
staticFollowup: 0089 final recovery_pending emits only current connection status/recipient/version plus matter/level, no grant lineage or retained saved-copy field ceiling. Need actual pg_restore regression. Candidate fix may enrich versioned journal facts with grant IDs and saved-copy field names, conservatively intersect old copies and reject legacy ambiguity; do not store private contents or broaden grants.
before: recovery-history-before.log:pg_dump/pg_restore resurrects narrowed saved fields and removed/regranted old copies.
fix: Migration0092 emits version2 grant lineage, saved field-name ceiling and withdrawn-review bound; replay intersects old state; ambiguous pending legacy updates quarantine instead of guessing.
tests: retention-recovery-after.log:17pass including2permission-history,7existing journal,8retention. Actual constrained non-superuser restore preserves unaffected third recipient and idempotence.

problem: runMigrations begins one transaction and takes transaction advisory lock, but many immutable SQL files contain their own BEGIN/COMMIT. First inner COMMIT ends the outer transaction, releases migration lock and commits DDL before checksum insert; crash/failure may leave applied schema without checksum, concurrent migrators can interleave.
next: Keep original migration bytes/checksums; normalize only supported transaction wrappers in runner with well-defined handling and real PostgreSQL rollback/concurrency regressions. Never edit applied files.
before: migration-atomicity-before.log:2fail: DDL survives checksum failure and another client acquires migration lock mid-batch.
fix: Remove only outer legacy BEGIN/COMMIT at execution time, preserve original bytes for SHA256; lexically reject unmanaged transaction controls without changing procedure bodies.
tests: migration-after.log:18pass across atomicity, SQL boundaries and runtime bootstrap; earlier whitespace-only expected-output error retained in migration-atomicity-after.log.
